ratings.reviewer_notes: Direct Htra3–TGF-beta cardiac fibrosis experiments are primarily pressure-overload/MI models; the human component is transcriptomic/proteomic analysis focused on IGFBP7 rather than direct human fibrosis testing.
Directly tests TGF-beta-induced profibrotic activation, collagen/fibronectin production, and myofibroblast transition in human cardiac fibroblasts.
Review concerns microglial neuroinflammation in cardiovascular disease and does not study TGF-beta signaling in human cardiac fibrosis.
Directly establishes dependence of cardiac fibrosis on myofibroblast TGF-beta receptor signaling, but exclusively in transgenic mouse models.
Links inhibition of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling to reduced myocardial fibrosis, but the experiments use rat and mouse models rather than humans.
Identifies noncanonical TGF-beta signaling as a regulator of profibrotic cardiac fibroblasts, with analogous cells found in patient tissue; the mechanistic evidence is mainly from animal models.
Review-level context on TGF-beta in cardiac remodeling and fibrosis, including observations in cardiomyopathy patients, but no direct original human study.
Includes human atrial tissue showing MG53 association with fibrosis, but manipulation of the TGF-beta1/Smad pathway and fibroblast phenotypes was performed in rat atrial fibroblasts.
Broad review of cardiac fibrosis mechanisms that discusses TGF-beta-family mediators; it does not directly test the relationship in humans.

Studies combined TGF-beta suppression and mechanosensing inhibition using public human/mouse datasets and engineered tissues, but the abstract does not clearly identify a direct human cardiac-fibrosis experiment.
Shows TGF-beta1-induced IL-11-dependent profibrotic responses in primary human fibroblasts, but their cardiac origin is not explicit; cardiac fibrosis causality is demonstrated in mice.
Directly treats human atrial fibroblasts from rheumatic-heart-disease patients with TGF-beta1 and relates CTGF expression to atrial fibrosis and remodeling.
Human failing-heart samples support EPRS/SULF1 relevance, while TGF-beta-stimulated fibroblast and cardiac-fibrosis mechanisms are not clearly demonstrated in human cardiac cells from the abstract.
Review describes TGF-beta-family activation of infarct myofibroblasts and post-MI fibrosis, but provides no direct original human testing.
Review-level discussion of oxidative stress, TGF-beta signaling, and cardiac remodeling/fibrosis in diabetic cardiomyopathy rather than a direct human study.
Directly studies TGFBR2 signaling and fibrogenic responses in human iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts and engineered heart tissues, with validation in cardiac tissue from DCM patients.
Directly establishes fibroblast TGF-beta receptor/Smad3 control of cardiac fibrosis, but all causal experiments are in genetically modified mice.
Review summarizes TGF-beta-mediated cardiac fibroblast activation and myocardial fibrosis in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; it is not an original direct human study.
Links exercise-mediated suppression of TGF-beta1/Smad signaling to reduced post-MI cardiac fibrosis, but uses mice and mouse-derived fibroblasts.
Directly examines TGF-beta3 expression in human post-MI fibrotic tissue and tests TGF-beta/Smad-dependent antifibrotic effects in human cardiac fibroblasts.
Review of cardiac-fibrosis pathogenesis that includes TGF-beta as a major mediator but does not directly study the relationship in humans.
Broad review of cardiac fibrosis and fibrogenic signaling, including TGF-beta, without direct original human experiments.
Directly tests TGF-beta receptor inhibition and fibrotic myofibroblast phenotypes in adult primary human ventricular cardiac fibroblasts and human iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts.
